newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain's Rojo links more rate cuts to CPI.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain's Rojo links more rate cuts to CPI.

text.p: Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Tuesday he sees room for further rate cuts if inflation remains on a downward trend.
"If inflation continues to fall, logically interest rates can be lowered carefully," Rojo said in a radio interview.
But other factors, including market jitters about the European monetary union, must also be considered in any decision to ease credit further, Rojo added.
He said there was some uncertainty as to when the European single currency would be launched.
"Germany has important economic and political problems in relation to the monetary union as other countries do and it is not totally clear how things will end," Rojo said.
Spain is well situated to fulfill the Maastricht Treaty convergence criteria for entry into the European economic and monetary union, he said.

"I think we will be able to comply comfortably with the inflation and fiscal criteria. We will see what happens but I think Spain is in shape to be in the first group of countries entering the monetary union."
